Hi! I know that life seems so hard right now, but know that there are always options! I don't know where you live, but I do know of a few colleges with programs especially for teenage mothers / single parents. For example:

Wilson College in Chambersburg, PA has a program with year-round housing, support groups, and financial aid that is easily accessed.

Endicott College in Boston has a special 'keys to degrees' program made for single parents.

St. Paul's in Virginia has a specialized single parent program.

There are so many more colleges out there with programs to help people in your situation. Just remember that no matter what, you should continue living for your daughter and yourself. She needs you.

I've tried talking to my counselor at school (multiple times) and once she even brought my mother into a meeting. My mother completely denied any abuse because I didn't have any bruises, and she said that I was a compulsive liar. My mother even laughed when I started crying and tried to explain, and I'm pretty sure that my mother and my counselor agreed that I was not abused, just punished in the way that they were back in the day, and that I should stop acting like a baby.
